name: the-library-and-records
title: The library, the records and the manuals
scope: Which document store serves which audience, who maintains each, and how something is promoted into a record. Excludes what makes an individual record good (see what-makes-a-good-record).

statements.statement: manuals = System manuals crews need to regularly do their job.
statements.context: Commenting on a transfer map that had moved the doctrine set into manuals.

statements.statement: library = Information, records of processes or learning that need to persist over time. particularly for humans
statements.context: Same comment, on the other store.

statements.statement: In summary: flighdeck/library = global documentation for all stakeholders and interested parties. .cockpit/records = the pilots most important and trusted records to enable them to do their job specifically and in isolation.
statements.context: Written advice, after the recon team confused the library with the pilot's records.

statements.statement: The library should be maintained by you, although other parties may write and read to/from it. This is the distinction, library is for all, records are yours.
statements.context: Same advice, on who owns each store.

statements.statement: The intention for you is not to replicate library documents but rather extract key findings and "record" them as research backed records, to guide the pilot in their tasks.
statements.context: Same advice, on what the pilot should do with library material.

statements.statement: Protect your records, they are source of truth, lasting across many sessions. The notepad stuff for things that probably won't matter in a few sessions."
statements.context: Order distinguishing records from scratch findings.

statements.statement: Promotion from notepad into records is the pathway. Accumulation of notepad entries may guide the creation of a researched record." Asked for the agent team protocol in CLAUDE.md.
statements.context: Order on how something becomes a record.

statements.statement: every good pilot protects their records. A source is good for official documentation. but for codebase sources... ensure only well researched (by special teammates) sources go in there for a purpose.
statements.context: Order on what may be cited as a source in a record.

statements.statement: library/terms.md: each build unit names its terms here. ensure all major system areas included
statements.context: Naming three more documents the rebuild should treat as interfaces.

statements.statement: operators manual: each unit describes how to "operate" that part of the machinery
maintenance manual: each unit describes how to "maintain" that part of the machinery
It appears the maintenance burden is increasing, the library and now the terms are your teammates. should you keep a maintenance JSON log to remind you of your maintenance tasks?
statements.context: Written advice on the growing number of documents the pilot keeps.
